jobs.title: Project Manager-Multiuse Facility Construction
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programs as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include program, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier program, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Job Description

About the Role

The Project Manager provides consulting services for our multi-use facility client account to help achieve the company's strategic business objectives.

This job is part of the Project Management function. They are responsible for the management of projects from initiation through completion. Projects consist of both ground up and facility infrastructure construction projects. Role may require up to 50% travel regionally predominantly in the Eastern Time Zone.

What You’ll Do

Manage all areas of project management for singular real estate projects. This includes planning, design, construction, occupancy, and closeout.

Work directly with clients to prepare all elements of the project. This includes the scope of work, project delivery resource requirements, cost estimates & budget, work plan schedule & milestones, quality control, and risk identification.

Define the project delivery resources from pre-qualified lists or through the project qualification process. Conduct a standard request for proposals, complete bid evaluations, and recommend resources to clients.

Implement project documentation governance that is aligned with company and client requirements.

Ensure project data integrity and documentation is accurate, timely, and coordinated.

Direct the project delivery team by providing guidance and direction to achieve goals.

Create action plans to meet objectives, budget, and schedule. Track the progress of each project and report status and variances.

Demonstrate ability to identify project threats and develop risk mitigation and contingency plans. Implement action plans to reduce or eliminate project risks.

Apply in-depth knowledge of standard principles and techniques/procedures to accomplish complex assignments and provide innovative solutions.

Coach others and share in-depth knowledge of own job discipline and broad knowledge of several job disciplines within the function.

Lead by example and model behaviors that are consistent with CBRE RISE (Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence) values. Work to build consensus and convince others to reach an agreement.

Impact a range of customer, operational, project, or service activities within own team and other related teams.

Qualifications

What You’ll Need

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future

Bachelor's Degree preferred with 5-8 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered. LEED AP, PMP, and/or CCM designation(s) preferred.
Ground up construction and MEP infrastructure experience is strongly desired.
Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook). Experience in Kahua or similar project management software and D365 or other Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform.
Organizational skills with an advanced inquisitive mentality.
Sophisticated math skills. Ability to calculate mildly complex figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial-related calculations.

Additional Information

SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change. We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.

Turner & Townsend does not accept any speculative or unsolicited CV’s that have been sent to our internal recruitment team or hiring managers from agencies outside of our preferred supplier list. Any speculative or unsolicited CV’s will be treated as a direct application.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

At BGBx
, we're driven by a simple idea: breakthrough thinking creates breakthrough impact. As an independent commercial solutions partner to pharmaceutical and life science companies, we bring together strategists, scientists, communicators, creatives, technologists, and data experts to tackle some of healthcare's most important challenges.

Our teams work across consulting and communications to help clients shape strategy, launch innovations, engage stakeholders, and drive meaningful results throughout the product lifecycle. The work is complex, fast-moving, and deeply connected to improving lives, creating opportunities for curious minds to make a real difference every day.

If you're energized by collaboration, inspired by innovation, and motivated by work that matters, you'll find a place to grow, contribute, and make a meaningful impact at BGBx.

Senior Project Manager

Position Overview

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for the overall management and administration of client projects throughout the entire project lifecycle. The Senior Project Manager is at the core of the team and helps everyone to communicate clearly while staying on time, on budget, and meets the highest of quality standards. This individual must demonstrate solid business judgment and sound strategic thinking. This role reports to the Director of Project Management.

Responsibilities: 

Understands the scope of work across an assigned account, as well as the project plan at an individual project level
Facilitates interdepartmental negotiation process to reach alignment on project resources and timelines
Aligns with Department Resource Managers to assign resources and ensure effective time management throughout a project life cycle
Continually monitors projects to ensure deliverables are on schedule and within scope
Collaborates with Account team to obtain client sign-off on project plans when needed
Prepares for all legal and regulatory submissions
Works closely with department leads on forecasting and future resource planning on assigned accounts
Builds partnerships and is persuasive/diplomatic in difficult situations
Ensures client requests are captured, executed, and exceed expectation
Partners with project stakeholders to ensure quality assurance standards and best practices are in place
Responsible for raising and maintaining awareness of all project issues and risks, and works with appropriate stakeholders to develop solutions
Expert in managing a high volume of work in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment
Acts as an internal hub of project information for assigned accounts
Maintains a proficient level of brand(s) knowledge

Qualifications

Proven track record of success in a fast-paced environment with the ability to quickly learn new technology
4+ years of project management experience, in pharmaceutical advertising or medical education
Expertise of project management techniques with a proven experience in people management, strategic planning, risk mitigation, hours and reporting
Ability to lead and manage multiple projects and project coordinators
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills
Ability to “think on your feet” and resolve issues quickly with little to no direction from supervisors; makes good judgments and renders solid decisions
Experience with the pharmaceutical business medical-legal regulations process preferred
Familiarity and proficiency with the principles of emotional intelligence
Excellent administrative and computer skills, with proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite and knowledge of basic project management software

S
alary Range:
$90,000 - $145,000 CAD

What We Offer

At BGBx, we invest in our people because exceptional talent drives exceptional work. We provide a competitive rewards package designed to support your health, well-being, professional growth, and life outside of work.

Our benefits package typically includes health care insurance, retirement plans, generous paid time off and holidays, wellness benefits, life insurance, learning and development opportunities, and other resources that support our employees throughout their careers. Additional benefits may be available based on your location. Beyond benefits, you'll find a culture built on collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on healthcare and the people it serves.

BGBx is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship status, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status or any category or class of person protected by law.

jobs.description:
As a member of the Business Systems team, you will lead the end-to-end delivery of SAP S/4HANA implementation initiatives across the Business Systems transformation portfolio.

This role ensures successful execution of program planning, delivery, testing, training, deployment, and adoption of SAP S/4HANA solutions across sites and functions. The SAP S/4HANA Project Manager drives governance, cross-functional alignment, and risk mitigation to ensure predictable outcomes and sustained business value.

Location:
Remote U.S.

Salary Range:
$136,700 - $182,300 plus bonus opportunity

Please note that the salary range information provided is a general guideline only. Criteria such as the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience, the scope of the specific position, as well as market and business considerations will be evaluated when extending an offer.

We Take Care Of Our People

Paid Time Off I
401K with Employer Match and Profit Sharing I
Health and Wellness Benefits I
Learning and Development Opportunities I
Referral Program I
Competitive Pay I
Recognition I
Employee Stock Purchase Plan I
Inclusive & Supportive Culture *

Your Challenge

Own the overall SAP S/4HANA program plan including scope, schedule, budget, risks, dependencies, and resource management
Lead integrated planning across process, technology, change management, data, and testing workstreams
Manage SAP implementation partners, internal teams, and functional leaders to ensure execution follows standards and governance
Coordinate business process alignment across Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Procurement, Engineering, and other domains
Drive issue resolution, risk identification, mitigation strategies, and leadership escalations
Ensure business readiness by collaborating with OCM, training, and readiness teams
Lead and coordinate all workshops with key resources
Oversee SIT, UAT, performance testing, and cutover validation for quality and traceability
Lead cutover planning and execution for a smooth transition into SAP S/4HANA
Track and report program progress, KPIs, and deliverables to leadership
Ensure alignment with related digital programs such as IBP, MES, PLM, QMS, CRM, and PPM
Business travel as needed

Key Working Relationships

Business Systems leadership; SAP partners; program and project managers; site and functional leaders; Business Process Owners (BPOs); OCM team; training and readiness teams; testing teams; enterprise architecture; data teams; SAP COE and change champions.

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Computer and Information Science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
7+ years of project management experience delivering large-scale ERP implementations, ideally SAP S/4HANA
Strong program management skills including planning, governance, scheduling, and coordination
Experience managing SAP Activate methodology and full S/4HANA lifecycle
Understanding of SAP functional domains such as FI/CO, MM, PP, SD, QM, PM, and IBP
Strong executive communication, stakeholder engagement, and influence capabilities
Experience working in matrixed and complex manufacturing environments
Experience leading and developing teams in a transformation environment
PMP, PMI-ACP, or SAP Activate certification preferred
Experience working in Aerospace and Defense preferred

Who We Are

Our Values

Environmental, Social and Governance

Curtiss-Wright's Defense Solution division is a trusted, proven leader, delivering superior products and services that meet the defense and aerospace industries' toughest challenges with best-in-class value. Our solutions address air, ground, and naval defense applications, and are focused on growth segments with a high demand for advanced technology, enhanced safety, security, and performance. As a leading Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) solutions supplier for battlefield platforms and communication systems, we are uniquely positioned to benefit from the DoD's commitment to maintaining technological superiority on the battlefield.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
LAKEORA is a Riyadh-based data and AI advisory firm and a pure-play Databricks partner. We build the governed data platforms that Saudi enterprises run their decisions on, going deep on one platform rather than wide across many, with governance designed in from the start. We are early-stage, flat, and deliberately small. You work directly with customers, own the architecture you design, and see it reach production. We like engineers who are direct, curious, and would rather get something right than get it agreed.

What are we looking for?

We're looking for an Senior Project Manager who owns the client relationship and keeps engagements moving: the single point of contact who handles escalations, drives approvals, and makes sure every deliverable lands.

At LAKEORA, this role sits at the center of the engagement. You'll be the bridge between client stakeholders and our technical team and leadership, turning delivery into something clients trust and want to expand. Lean team, high visibility, real impact.

Key Responsibilities

Own the client relationship across the engagement lifecycle, serving as the primary point of contact from kickoff through delivery and handover
Manage scope, timelines, and resourcing across one or more concurrent client engagements
Handle escalations directly, keeping client stakeholders and the Lakeora team aligned when issues arise
Run approval workflows: scope sign-offs, change requests, milestone acceptance, and deliverable reviews
Own engagement documentation: SOWs, status reports, meeting notes, decision logs, and delivery artifacts
Lead steering committee and status meetings, translating technical progress into business language for client leadership
Track engagement health (budget, burn rate, risks, dependencies) and surface issues before they escalate
Coordinate across data engineers, platform engineers, and solutions architects to keep delivery on track
Identify follow-on and expansion opportunities within accounts, working with the team to shape them

Qualifications

Required

4+ years in project management, delivery management, or technical project management, ideally in data, cloud, or consulting
Proven track record managing client-facing technical delivery from scope through acceptance
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to handle escalations and hard conversations calmly
Solid understanding of data platform projects and modern data and cloud concepts (you don't need to code, but you need to speak the language)
Experience managing scope, budget, timelines, and risk across concurrent engagements
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level reporting and disciplined documentation
Comfortable in a lean, high-ownership team where you wear multiple hats
Fluent English; Arabic strongly valued for KSA client engagements

Preferred

Experience delivering Databricks, data platform, or analytics and AI projects
Familiarity with the Databricks ecosystem (Lakehouse, Unity Catalog, delivery on cloud hyperscalers)
Consulting background at a data and AI advisory or systems integrator
PMP, PRINCE2, or Agile/Scrum certification preferred
Sector exposure in Industrial (Manufacturing & Oil and Gas), Logistics & Transportation, or Insurance
Presales or account growth experience

If this sounds like the kind of work you want to do, we would like to hear from you. LAKEORA is an equal opportunity employer and assesses every application on merit.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
About Onit

We're redefining the future of legal operations through the power of AI. Our cutting-edge platform streamlines enterprise legal management, matter management, spend management and contract lifecycle processes, transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated solutions.

We’re a team of innovators using AI at the core
to help legal departments become faster, smarter, and more strategic. As we continue to grow and expand the capabilities of our new AI-centric platform, we’re looking for bold thinkers and builders who are excited to shape the next chapter of legal tech.

If you're energized by meaningful work, love solving complex problems, and want to help modernize how legal teams operate, we’d love to meet you.

Position Summary

As an Implementation Manager, you’ll be responsible for delivering successful client projects by blending project management expertise, technical execution, and client partnership. You’ll work directly with clients to uncover requirements, configure workflows, and implement integrations such as APIs and flat-file based finance exchanges. jobs.title: Senior Manager - Carbon-Free Energy Project manager
jobs.description:
Role Overview

Nscale is scaling AI infrastructure across the United States, and the energy that powers it is now the company’s largest sustainability lever and one of its biggest commercial differentiators. The Senior Manager, & Carbon-Free Energy will own the roadmap for sourcing carbon-free energy (CFE) across Nscale’s U.S. portfolio and lead its core environmental strategy.

The role pairs two mandates. First, find, evaluate and help close the energy deals that decarbonize Nscale’s load: PPAs, virtual PPAs, utility green tariffs, energy attribute certificates and emerging firm clean sources such as advanced nuclear, geothermal and storage-backed renewables. Second, lead strategy on water, embodied carbon and the emissions Nscale produces from its own operations.

The role partners closely with Power/Utility, Site Development, Finance, Legal and Commercial teams, carries direct people-leadership responsibility and is designed to scale as Nscale grows.

Key Responsibilities

Carbon-Free Energy Strategy & Procurement
Own Nscale’s carbon-free energy (CFE) strategy and roadmap, setting portfolio targets by U.S. market and site type
Partner with Power/Utility and Commercial teams to originate, structure, negotiate and close clean energy transactions, including physical and virtual PPAs, utility green tariffs and sleeved supply, and renewable energy certificates (RECs).
Build business cases including financial models for price, basis, shape and volume risk, contract tenor, and credit and collateral requirements.
Run energy due diligence during site selection: grid carbon intensity, local CFE supply, utility and market structure, interconnection timelines, and regulatory barriers to clean supply.
Represent Nscale with utilities, independent power producers, developers, brokers and regulators; build a pipeline of offtake opportunities in each U.S. market where Nscale operates.
Manage the contracted CFE portfolio after signing, tracking project delivery, contract performance and development risk on multi-year deals.
Emerging & Firm Clean Energy Sources
Scan and evaluate emerging firm and dispatchable clean sources, including advanced nuclear and SMRs, next-generation geothermal, long-duration storage, hydro, and low-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and RNG.
Assess technology readiness, cost curves, timelines and counterparty risk
Evaluate on-site and adjacent generation, behind-the-meter and co-location structures, microgrids and battery storage with Engineering and Power teams.
Develop grid-interactivity and demand flexibility options, such as load shifting, demand response and backup-generation alternatives, that lower emissions and ease interconnection.
Track U.S. energy policy and market rules (for example federal clean energy tax credits, state clean energy standards and ISO/RTO market rules) and their effect on Nscale’s sourcing options.
Build relationships with clean energy developers, industry groups and buyer coalitions to keep Nscale early in the deal flow.
Resource & Environmental Strategy
Lead water stewardship strategy: consumption baselines, cooling technology decisions and replenishment initiatives.
Lead the inventory of emissions Nscale produces directly from its own operations (such as backup generators, on-site fuel use and refrigerants) and drive plans to reduce them.
Stakeholder Engagement & Team Leadership
Shape accurate, defensible sustainability and energy messaging for executives, clients, investors, communities and policymakers.
Collaborate with community affairs, public policy, and other internal teams on energy and environmental matters.
Directly manage and develop the team, and build the function’s planning cadence, governance and future subject-matter roles (e.g. energy markets).

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, energy, environmental science, business, finance or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years in sustainability, energy procurement, renewable project development or energy markets, including experience negotiating or structuring energy or clean energy agreements (PPAs, VPPAs, utility tariffs or RECs).
Working knowledge of U.S. power markets (e.g. ERCOT, PJM, MISO), utility regulation, transmission and interconnection, and renewable energy certificate markets.
Experience with financial modeling of energy deals and assessment of price, volume and development risk.
Experience managing people or leading cross-functional programs with executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or advanced degree in energy, environmental policy or finance.
Track record of closing utility-scale clean energy deals (wind, solar, storage) or firm clean energy offtakes (nuclear, geothermal, hydro).
Experience at a hyperscaler, colocation provider, utility, IPP or energy advisory firm serving data center load.
Familiarity with 24/7 CFE and hourly matching methods and granular certificates.
Experience with carbon removal buyers or environmental attribute suppliers.
Direct experience with public utility commissions, regulators or grid operators, and with multi-state portfolios across U.S. markets.
Willingness to travel ~20%.

Job Title
: Senior Program Manager
Location:
Remote with occasional travel to customer sites (US-wide) or Ten One Aerospace (Annapolis, MD) facilities as needed.

About Ten One Aerospace

Ten One Aerospace provides engineering services and products for the aerospace industry,
specializing in astrodynamics, controls, and autonomy for space missions. Our focus is on
spacecraft GNC systems and flight software (FSW). Ten One Aerospace is developing a full
suite of GNC capabilities for space missions, including RPO and docking across all orbital
regimes.

Spacecraft RPO is a challenging, highly specialized, multidisciplinary field of aerospace
engineering, extending beyond traditional GNC, and it is critical to space missions such as debris
removal, on-orbit servicing, refueling, and in-space manufacturing. At Ten One Aerospace, we
aim to make RPO safe and affordable to lower the entry barriers for new space companies and
enable a robust space economy.

When you join Ten One Aerospace, you’ll be a vital part of a passionate and supportive team
dedicated to pushing the frontiers of aerospace technology. You’ll be empowered and given
autonomy to propose improvements or innovations based on your observations and expertise.

Our culture thrives on mentorship and intellectual growth as we seek to build a team of world-
class experts on this critical skill set of spacefaring tomorrow.

Position Overview

Ten One Aerospace is seeking a Senior Program Manager who is excited to apply their
experience to customer-facing projects at an innovative space company. As a Senior PM you will
have responsibility, accountability, and authority to plan and execute projects that develop and
deliver Ten One’s Rendezvous Proximity Operations (RPO) Kits and other Guidance,
Navigation, and Control (GNC) capabilities to our customers. You will provide coordination and
leadership to cross-functional internal teams, external suppliers, and subcontractors. You will
own all aspects of your projects and be the TOA focal responsible for ensuring customer
satisfaction aligned with the scope of firm fixed price and time & materials contracts.

Responsibilities

Orchestrate the day-to-day execution of programs involving spacecraft payload design,

assembly, integration, testing and delivery, including both hardware and software.
Negotiate realistic program schedules and budgets, and continually track to on-time and

on-cost program execution.
Coordinate with internal teams such as systems engineering, GNC, flight software,

hardware, finance, contracts, and the project management office (PMO) to ensure
successful cross-functional program execution.
Lead efforts to identify and manage subcontractors, consultants, and vendors to support

your programs.
Build strong working relationships with customer teams and collaboratively work to

define and execute well-structured firm fixed price and time & materials contracts.
Continuously monitor and mitigate scope creep.
Contribute to project management and PMO process improvement efforts, focusing on

right-sized efficiency and building a strong foundation to support company growth.
Mentor junior team members in areas such as project management best practices and

effective communication practices.

Required Qualifications

10+ years managing technical projects and programs, preferably in the aerospace

industry, and at least partially at small companies or startups.
Bachelor's degree, preferably in a technical field (aerospace, software, systems,

mechanical, or other engineering).
PMP, MBA or other formal management training preferred.
Experience managing costs on firm fixed price contracts using tools such as EVM.
Experience with formal risk and opportunity management processes.
Familiarity with contracts and their implications on project execution such as intellectual

property, security/IT/QMS flow downs, export control, etc.
Experience with contract and statement of work negotiations.
Experience developing ground-up program BOEs that consider labor, hardware

components, external consultant/vendor expenses, travel, etc.
Experience developing integrated master schedules for technical programs.
Desire to work in a small, fast-paced, and innovative aerospace company.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work with multidisciplinary and distributed teams
Must be authorized to work in the USA without sponsorship. Current security clearances

or ability to obtain clearances is a plus.

Desired Skills

Experience with projects that have qualified hardware for space flight. For example,

awareness of topics related to conformal coating, vibration testing, TVAC testing, etc.
Experience with projects involving visual and IR spectrum optics. For example, FOD

mitigation, focusing procedures, etc.
Experience with projects involving software for on-orbit applications.
Experience managing both project and product organizations.

Why Ten One Aerospace?

At Ten One Aerospace, you’ll join a team of innovative professionals dedicated to pushing the
frontiers of space technology. Our culture fosters intellectual growth, mentorship, and continuous
learning in an environment where your contributions matter. If you're looking for an exciting,
fast-paced career where you can make a real impact, this is the opportunity for you.

As a member of the Ten One Aerospace team, you’ll enjoy opportunities for career development
with some of the most reputable professionals in the industry, a comprehensive benefits package,
including health, vision and dental insurance options for you and your family, 401K and HSA
plans, and paid-time-off. The salary range for this opportunity is $120,000-$239,000 based on
experience and location.

Ready to launch your career to new heights? Apply now and join us in shaping the
future of space technology! To apply, head to Ten One Aerospace's Careers page, or submit a resume, cover letter, and salary requirements to careers@primaveratalent.com
.

jobs.title: Global Capacity & Resilience Program Manager
jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Everpure's global contract manufacturing network needs a single owner for capacity governance and supply chain network resilience — someone who replaces fragmented, reactive decision-making with one coherent framework spanning all lines of business. This role sits at the center of that shift: building the governance structures, risk frameworks, and executive reporting that let the network absorb shocks — geopolitical, infrastructure, business continuity — without derailing growth targets. You'll work closely with the Network Design Council, site managers, CM partners, and cross-functional teams like Mfg Product & Test Engineering, R&D Engineering, and Indirect Sourcing, with real influence over how capacity and risk decisions get made across the network.

What You'll Do

Own and govern the Global Capacity Planning Framework, building the RACI that gives the Supply Chain Network Council one source of truth across all lines of business
Serve as the central escalation point for capacity issues network-wide, running a Monthly Global Capacity Review and standardized dashboards that keep site managers and CM partners aligned
Define and govern Time to Recover (TTR) and Time to Survive/Time to Fail (TTF) resilience KPIs across all global production sites and products, translating gaps into prioritized mitigation plans for the highest-risk sites
Drive the Capacity Analysis Tool and executive Tableau dashboard roadmap, and own the capital budget that funds capacity and resilience investments against growth targets
Partner with Indirect Sourcing and Engineering to optimize test process & time, landed cost through data research, common infrastructure parts and improved CM pricing and forecasting

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Operations Research, Supply Chain, or related field; Master’s degree preferred. Six Sigma Green Belt certification or above preferred.
An industrial process engineering mindset — comfortable applying process analysis, simulation, optimization/heuristics, or forecasting to translate operational data (cost, service, capability, emissions) into network design decisions.
Proven ability to lead complex, technically-oriented transformation projects, utilizing methodologies like Waterfall, Agile, or Scrum to manage scope, schedules, and deliverables in a dynamic environment, paired with exceptional communication and negotiation skills to translate technical/data concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build consensus across supply chain, IT, and engineering teams.
Deep fluency in global contract manufacturing capacity planning, built through experience designing governance frameworks, RACIs, and executive review cadences that hold up across a complex, matrixed network
Strong analytical capability — comfortable building capacity models and KPI dashboards in tools like Tableau, and partnering with BI/analytics teams on executive-facing reporting
Experience building supply chain risk and resilience programs, including business continuity planning, scenario analysis, and recovery metrics such as Time to Recover and Time to Survive/Fail
Skilled at driving alignment across cross-functional, matrixed teams without direct authority — able to influence site managers, CM partners, and senior stakeholders toward a shared framework
We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Santa Clara, CA office in compliance with Everpure's policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave.

Salary ranges are determined based on role, level and location. For positions open to candidates in multiple geographical locations, the base salary range is reflective of the labor market across the applicable locations.

This role may be eligible for incentive pay and/or equity.

There is no application deadline and we accept applications on an ongoing basis until the job is filled.

The Annual Base Salary Range Is

$153,000—$230,000 USD

What You Can Expect From Us

Innovation: We celebrate those who think critically, like a challenge, and aspire to be trailblazers.
Growth: We give you the space and support to grow along with us and to contribute to something meaningful. We have been named Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology™, Fortune's Best Workplaces in the Bay Area™, and certified as a Great Place to Work®!
Team: We build each other up and set aside ego for the greater good.

And because we understand the value of bringing your full and best self to work, we offer a variety of perks to manage a healthy balance, including flexible time off, wellness resources, and company-sponsored team events. Check out http://benefits.everpuredata.com/ for more information.

Accommodations And Accessibility

That’s why we are committed to fostering the growth and development of every person, cultivating a sense of community through our Employee Resource Groups and advocating for inclusive leadership.

jobs.title: Software Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Efficient Computer is rethinking computing from the ground up to solve one of AI's biggest challenges: energy. Our Fabric architecture delivers a 10–100x improvement in energy efficiency for general-purpose computation, including AI, while supporting familiar programming languages and software frameworks—unlocking new possibilities for autonomous machines, intelligent infrastructure, wearables, and space systems. With our first processor, Electron E1, now shipping in volume and more than $97 million in Series B financing recently announced, we're accelerating customer deployments and scaling our architecture to data center performance. Join us to build the hardware and software that bring intelligence wherever it's needed and help shape the next generation of computing.

Efficient Computer is building the next generation of super-efficient, general-purpose processors around the Fabric architecture, a novel spatial dataflow design. The Fabric is only as useful as the software that targets it: the effcc compiler, the system software stack (optimization libraries such as eff-dsp and, over time, the runtime), and the SDK that customers build on.

We are looking for a Software Technical Program Manager to own the quarterly release of this software, from scoping and commitment through code freeze, qualification, and ship. You will be the operational center of the software program: building and defending the release plan, driving the critical path, holding the quality bar, and making tradeoff conversations happen before something slips. You will work daily with the compiler, system software, embedded, and product teams, and regularly interface with architecture and hardware teams especially when it comes time to bring-up new silicon.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Release

Own the execution of the quarterly software release from planning through ship: the schedule, critical path, and delivery. Product defines what ships and why, Engineering determines what is feasible, and you are accountable for when and how it lands. Each release bundles the SDK, the effcc compiler, optimized software libraries, and eventually the runtime.
Build the release plan with product managers, team leads, and engineering managers. This includes feature commitments, freeze dates, qualification windows, and ship criteria, informed by Product's customer requirements and the hardware schedule.
Drive the weekly execution cadence (release reviews, bug triage, go/no-go) and maintain a single source of truth for status, dependencies, and decisions.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

Coordinate handoffs across the compiler, system software, and embedded teams, and with architecture, product and hardware teams.
Keep Product Management informed about execution and raise risks accordingly that could affect the release schedule, quality, or feature-set.
Manage the release's dependency chains: e.g. compiler features that libraries depend on, interfaces shared between the SDK and the runtime, LLVM and toolchain versions, board and silicon availability, etc.

Maintain Release Quality

Establish with our teams release quality gates: e.g. no regressions in cycles, energy, or code size on the benchmark suites relative to the previous release; test coverage thresholds met, etc.

Run the release checklist (the gates above plus documentation, release notes, etc.), working with the release shepherd to hold owners to closure criteria.

Track escaped defects and feed what we learn back into the checklist.

Manage Risk, Decisions, and Reporting

Surface risk early with mitigation options and schedule impact quantified: e.g. late compiler features, coverage shortfalls, and benchmark regressions.
Facilitate scope, schedule, and quality tradeoffs, and document what was decided, by whom, and why.
Deliver executive reporting: where the release stands, what is at risk, what decision is needed and by when.

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent; M.S. or MBA a plus.
7+ years in software engineering or program management, including prior hands-on engineering experience in compilers, systems software, or embedded software.
Working fluency in using AI-tools to facilitate program management – from reporting, to issue tracking, to dependency analysis and more.
Strong experience with the software delivery flow: compiler toolchains, embedded SDKs, CI/CD, test coverage, performance benchmarking, and release engineering.
Demonstrated ability to build and defend a bottoms-up schedule with critical path analysis and dependency mapping.
Track record influencing without authority: earning the technical credibility to push senior engineers on commitments and dates.
Strong written and verbal communication; able to run a room of principal engineers and an executive review with equal effectiveness.
Hands-on with program tooling: Github, Linear, Jira, Notion, Confluence, CI systems, etc.

Desired Qualifications & Experience Requirements

Experience as the technical program manager on a first-generation silicon product, where the toolchain and hardware matured together.
Familiarity with LLVM or MLIR, machine learning compilers, or language runtimes.
Knowledge of dataflow, spatial, or other novel compute architectures.
Experience managing pre-silicon software enablement against emulation or FPGA prototyping programs.

We offer a competitive base salary for this role, generally ranging from $200,000 to $260,000, plus a 10% annual bonus, meaningful equity, and comprehensive benefits. Final compensation will depend on experience, level, and location, with flexibility for the right candidate.

Why Join Efficient?

Build what's next. At Efficient, you'll tackle big challenges with room to take ownership and make an impact. We back you with competitive pay, equity, a 401(k) match, company-paid benefits, paid parental leave, and flexibility—plus opportunities to grow your skills and career as we scale.

jobs.description:
Description

The Technical Program Manager (TPM), Technology Integration & Support is responsible for the end-to-end onboarding, integration, and deployment of automation vendor technologies (AGVs, AMRs, autonomous floor care, etc.) across Amazon's fulfillment and sortation network. This role serves as the primary technical liaison between external vendors and internal Amazon stakeholders — ensuring that all vendor technologies meet Amazon's network, security, and compliance standards before deployment.

Key job responsibilities

Vendor Technology Onboarding (40%)

Own the full lifecycle of vendor IT onboarding for AGV/AMR and automation technologies — from initial kick-off through production deployment
Conduct technical kick-off meetings with vendor engineering teams to review Amazon IT requirements (network architecture, security, IoT device standards)
Guide vendors through Amazon's onboarding documentation process: network diagrams, IT overview questionnaires, data element inventories, and wireless device assessment forms
Manage 4–5 concurrent vendor onboarding projects at steady state; scale to 10+ during peak periods
Track onboarding status across all active vendors using Asana and/or SmartSheet dashboards

Network Architecture & Configuration (20%)

Review and approve vendor network diagrams for compliance with Amazon network standards
Configure VLANs, assign static IPs, generate PPSKs (pre-shared keys) for WiFi 802.11ax connectivity
Coordinate ACL port configurations and firewall rule deployments with local IT and network engineering teams
Validate that vendor IoT devices operate within approved frequency bands, protocols, and power levels

Security & Compliance (15%)

Manage Third-Party Security (TPS) assessments with Amazon InfoSec — submit tickets, gather vendor responses, track remediation
Author and submit ANOW (Access Network Operations Workflow) requests for vendor network access
Coordinate IoT device certification through Amazon's hardware qualification pipeline
Ensure vendor technologies meet mTLS, SSO, and SiteConnect/VPN requirements before go-live

Technical Assessments & Documentation (10%)

Author formal Vendor Technical Assessment reports evaluating integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness
Document conditional approvals, pilot constraints, and scaling requirements for each technology
Maintain a centralized knowledge base of approved devices, network configurations, and onboarding playbooks

Infrastructure Deployment Coordination (10%)

Coordinate physical infrastructure work with general contractors (GCs) — network rack installation, LVC/power cabling, IPC housing, fire alarm panel integration
Develop and distribute BOMs (Bills of Materials) for site-level technology deployments
Establish and run weekly coordination meetings for multi-site rollouts

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management (5%)

Serve as the single-threaded owner for vendor IT integration across legal, category management, IT security, safety, demand intake, and local IT teams
Manage escalations from site teams, EU/international stakeholders, and Amazon leadership
Provide regular status updates to program leadership on vendor onboarding pipeline health

A day in the life

A Day in the Life

Every Day As a Technical Program Manager On The Technology Integration & Support Team Brings a Dynamic Mix Of Technical Problem-solving, Vendor Collaboration, And Cross-functional Coordination. Here’s What a Typical Day Looks Like

You start your morning by reviewing your Asana and Taskei dashboards to check the status of 4–5 active vendor onboarding projects. You flag any blockers — maybe a vendor’s network diagram needs revisions before it can be approved, or a Third-Party Security (TPS) assessment is awaiting InfoSec feedback. You prioritize your day around what will keep these projects moving forward.

By mid-morning, you’re leading a technical kick-off call with a new AGV vendor’s engineering team. You walk them through Amazon’s IT requirements — network standards, security protocols, IoT device certification — and outline the onboarding documentation they’ll need to complete. You answer their questions about VLAN configurations, WiFi 802.11ax connectivity, and mTLS requirements, translating Amazon’s standards into actionable steps for the vendor.

After lunch, you shift into hands-on technical work. You review a vendor’s submitted network diagram for compliance, configure VLAN assignments and static IPs for an upcoming pilot site, and generate PPSKs for wireless device connectivity. You coordinate with the local IT team on ACL port configurations and firewall rules that need to be deployed before the vendor’s equipment arrives on-site.

In the afternoon, you join a weekly coordination meeting for a multi-site robotics rollout. You provide updates on the technology integration workstream, review the Bill of Materials for the next site, and align with general contractors on network rack installation timelines. After the meeting, you draft a Vendor Technical Assessment report evaluating a new automation technology’s integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness.

Throughout the day, you’re the single-threaded owner connecting the dots between vendors, site teams, IT security, legal, and program leadership. You might field an escalation from a European site team about a connectivity issue, submit an ANOW request for vendor network access, or update leadership on the health of your vendor onboarding pipeline. No two days are exactly the same, but every day centers on making sure the right technology gets integrated safely, securely, and on schedule.

About The Team

The GESA Development Engineering Automation Team is here to help provide Automated Solutions for projects ranging from AGV Tugger Systems and Floor Cleaning AMRs to Automated Turret Trucks and beyond. Our team is responsible for standardizing and qualifying Automated Vehicle Systems for use within Amazon Facilities, both retrofitted Automation Packages as well as Green Field Designs for future Facility Generations.

Basic Qualifications

2+ years of technical program management experience
2+ years of work in large-scale networking environments experience
Knowledge of project management tools and software
Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Management, Information Systems, or other related discipline

Experience managing external vendor relationships in a technical capacity

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in quality assurance/testing/mobile industry/internet of things (IoT)
Experience in one or more of the following: application security frameworks, security code reviews, incident response, security infrastructure, penetration testing, mobile security, cloud security, AI security, identity and access controls
Experience in automation or monitoring frameworks, deployment or development
Knowledge of operating systems, hardware, storage, network, security, database administration and cloud infrastructure
Experience working in fulfillment center, warehouse, or industrial automation environments

jobs.description:
Description

Northland Controls is seeking an experienced Embedded Program Manager in Sunnyvale, CA. This is an exciting opportunity for a proven security industry professional who enjoys working closely with enterprise customers, leading global service programs, developing high-performing teams, and continuously improving service delivery.

In this role, you will be embedded within a key enterprise customer account, serving as a trusted program partner and primary point of coordination between the customer and Northland Controls. You will lead a multidisciplinary embedded team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with program requirements and customer priorities.

You will maintain regular touch points with the global team, review and verify work, provide monthly program updates, partner with customer leadership on challenges and opportunities, and lead quarterly business reviews focused on KPIs, SLAs, priorities, and continuous improvement. You will also be accountable for the performance and development of each team member and for making resource or team adjustments when delivery expectations are not being met.

If you're looking for an opportunity to become deeply integrated with a global customer program, strengthen service delivery, develop talented teams, and make a measurable impact in a growing organization, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Serve as the embedded program leader within a key enterprise customer account, developing a strong understanding of the customer's organization, security program, priorities, standards, operating model, and long-term objectives.
Maintain daily or regular touch points with the global embedded team to review priorities, verify work, remove blockers, and ensure services are being delivered in accordance with program requirements.
Act as the primary point of contact between the customer and Northland Controls for program-level planning, performance, communication, escalation, and issue resolution.
Partner closely with customer management on strategic focus areas, active projects, delivery improvements, program challenges, opportunities, and the ongoing evolution of the program.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team that may include Project Managers, consultants, systems technicians, and engineers, fostering a collaborative and high-performing work environment.
Establish clear expectations for each team member and hold individuals accountable for performance, service quality, responsiveness, and delivery commitments.
Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, mentorship, and direction; manage performance improvement and corrective action in accordance with Northland processes, and recommend team adjustments when sustained improvement is not achieved.
Allocate and prioritize resources across projects, operational needs, and customer initiatives while balancing workloads and optimizing utilization, productivity, and coverage.
Track program performance using KPIs, SLAs, delivery milestones, workload data, and other relevant metrics; identify trends and take action when performance is at risk.
Prepare and deliver regular program updates to customer stakeholders and Northland leadership, including performance, resource, financial, risk, and improvement reporting.
Lead the development and presentation of Quarterly Business Reviews, coordinating team inputs, reporting against KPIs and SLAs, collecting customer feedback, aligning on quarterly priorities, and driving follow-through on agreed actions.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, proactively managing expectations, addressing concerns, and supporting strong satisfaction and confidence in the team's services.
Track and analyze relationship and service indicators, including stakeholder feedback, responsiveness, recurring concerns, and service-quality trends, to assess the effectiveness of program delivery and relationship management.
Identify program risks, dependencies, and issues; develop mitigation plans and work with customer management and Northland leadership to proactively address challenges and keep delivery on track.
Manage the overall embedded team budget, monitor expenditures and forecasts, identify budget risks, and provide monthly financial and accrual reporting as required.
Conduct regular quality reviews of team outputs and service delivery to ensure work aligns with customer requirements, established standards, and program expectations.
Drive continuous improvement by analyzing scheduling, workload, performance, and service data to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities to improve delivery processes and outcomes.
Coordinate across internal teams, customer stakeholders, program peers, suppliers, and dependency partners to align delivery, share best practices, and ensure seamless integration of work across the program.
Gather and analyze feedback from customer stakeholders and team members and translate that feedback into practical improvements to services, processes, team performance, and working relationships.
Proactively identify and resolve conflicts, facilitating practical solutions and timely escalation when issues require additional leadership involvement.
Conduct periodic program evaluations and lessons-learned reviews to assess outcomes, document improvements, and inform future program planning and service strategy.
Travel to customer locations and team sites as required.

What We're Looking For

Significant experience managing complex enterprise programs, embedded services, or technical service-delivery teams within the security industry or a closely related technical environment.
Proven experience working directly with enterprise customers and managing long-term customer relationships in a high-visibility, service-oriented environment.
Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, including direct accountability for individual performance and service delivery.
Strong experience with KPI and SLA management, executive-level program reporting, Quarterly Business Reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Strong understanding of program financial management, budgeting, forecasting, accrual reporting, resource planning, workload balancing, and cost controls.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, dependencies, and competing requirements within a large global customer environment.
Strong knowledge of physical security systems and services, including access control, video surveillance, and related enterprise technologies.
Experience with Lenel, Software House, or similar enterprise security platforms; relevant certifications are highly desirable.
PMP certification or equivalent program or project management credentials preferred.
Excellent leadership, communication, presentation, facilitation, and organizational skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and senior customer stakeholders.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, anticipate risks, navigate changing priorities, and drive issues through resolution.
Ability to build productive, trusted relationships with customers, colleagues, suppliers, and business partners while operating effectively as both a customer-facing partner and a representative of Northland Controls.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel as required.

Why Join Northland Controls?

At Northland Controls, you'll have the opportunity to become an integral part of a key enterprise customer's global security program while leading the people, processes, and performance that support consistent service delivery. You'll work alongside experienced customer, project, engineering, and operations professionals while helping strengthen the teams and operating practices that support our continued growth.

We value innovation, accountability, collaboration, and doing what it takes to deliver exceptional results for our customers. As an Embedded Program Manager, you'll have the opportunity to build lasting customer partnerships, develop your team, improve how services are delivered, and make a meaningful impact across the organization.

Northland Controls offers competitive compensation, comprehensive health and retirement benefits, professional development opportunities, and a flexible working environment.

jobs.title: Founding Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

On our largest global rollouts, connectivity is what makes or breaks the program.

These customers run several ERP systems across many entities and countries, with interfaces, master data and process variants that have grown over decades. Whether blp is usable on day one, and whether the first go-live holds its date, depends more on getting that landscape right than on almost anything else. You are the person who makes sure it is right. You sit opposite the customer's enterprise architects and IT leads, understand what their landscape actually does rather than what the documentation says, and shape the technical solution with them.

Getting this right is relentless project management as much as architecture. Requirements on a landscape this size never arrive clear. You chase them until they are: pushing the customer's IT organization for answers, going back when an answer is vague, and refusing to let an assumption stand in for a decision. You spot the major developments and the roadblocks early, while there is still time to do something about them, and you put them in front of the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee rather than discovering them in test.

When you raise something, you bring the way through it. You prepare the discussion with the customer, make the implications clear in their language, and come with options. "We cannot do that and we will miss the go-live" is not the job. Working out what would make it possible, and what it costs, is. Where something exceeds the standard you prepare the decision rather than take it alone: options, effort, consequences, and a clear recommendation for the steering committee or for our engineering leadership.

You are the strong technical counterpart for the customer's IT organization and for the Senior Project Manager. Both rely on you to know what is actually true. You work primarily up to the first go-live, where the solution design is either right or expensive, and you are staffed by process and landscape complexity rather than by deal size.

A word on what you build.
Our integration layer works like an iPaaS: connections are assembled as configuration on our own platform, specific to that customer, rather than written as code. You work in that layer yourself, so this is a hands-on role, and you document what you have configured so that the next person can understand and maintain it. What you do not do is write code that ships with the product. That distinction is what keeps a customer-specific solution from quietly becoming everyone's problem.

Two roles sit either side of you and the handoffs are clean.

With the Integrations Engineer:
you define what the connection has to do and why, they build and operate it at that customer and own whether it runs. You hand them a specification, they come back with questions and constraints from the real system, and you resolve them together. When something breaks in their environment, it is theirs. When something is wrong in what was asked for, it is yours.

With the Product Engineer:
when a requirement cannot be met in configuration, or when the same requirement has now appeared at the third customer, you make the case for building it into the product. You write the specification, they build it, and you are the one who confirms it actually solves the customer problem it came from. After that it is part of the standard and you configure against it like anything else.

Key Responsibilities

Shape the technical solution with the customer, including their enterprise architects and IT leads.
Turn business requirements into a clear, implementable specification.
Drive requirements to clarity, relentlessly. Chase the customer's IT organization until an answer is specific enough to build on.
Configure integrations on our platform where the standard covers it, and document what you have configured.
Identify precisely where the standard does not cover a requirement, and judge whether it belongs in configuration or in the product.
Identify major development needs and technical roadblocks early, and escalate them to the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee while there is still time.
Prepare those discussions with the customer: make the implications clear, and bring options rather than a refusal.
Prepare scope decisions with options, effort and consequences, and bring a clear recommendation to the steering committee or to our engineering leadership.
Specify what the Integrations Engineer builds at the customer, and resolve the constraints they bring back from the real system.
Make the case for what should be built once for everyone, hand it to our Product Engineers with a proper specification, and confirm it solves the problem it came from.
Support the Senior Project Manager and Project Manager on technical feasibility, effort and sequencing.
Stay on the account through the first go-live, and hand over a solution design that is documented and maintainable.
Feed recurring customer requirements back to Product so the standard grows in the right direction.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

Relentless on Clarity – You do not accept a vague answer as an answer, and you keep going until the requirement is specific enough to build on.
Architectural Judgment – You can tell the difference between a requirement that deserves a custom solution and one that deserves a conversation.
Credibility with Architects – You hold your own with a customer's enterprise architect and earn their trust rather than deferring to them.
Clear Recommendations – You frame a difficult scope question so that the people who decide can actually decide, and you say plainly what you would do.
Translation – You move between a business requirement and a technical design in both directions without losing anything.
Long-Term Thinking – You design for what the customer will need in two years, not only for what unblocks the current wave.

What You Bring

Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
4+ years of experience in solution design, technical consulting, enterprise integration or a technical product role.
Solid understanding of enterprise system landscapes: ERP systems, interfaces, master data, and how data actually moves between them.
Hands-on experience configuring integrations on an integration platform, or comparable low-code or configuration-driven work.
Experience writing specifications that engineers can build from without a translation layer.
Track record of driving technical clarity in a project setting, including escalating early and constructively.
Comfortable in customer-facing technical discussions with senior IT stakeholders.
Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.
Bonus points for hands-on experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or comparable ERP systems, or with e-invoicing and EDI standards.

Benefits

High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.
Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.
Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.
Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.
Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.
Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.
Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.
Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation?
Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at https://blp.digital/company/careers.

Job Context

HC Group Co., Ltd. is seeking an experienced and responsible Factory Security Manager
to oversee and strengthen the overall security operations of its factories and other company premises. The position will be responsible for security planning, risk assessment, security personnel supervision, access control, asset protection, incident management, emergency response and coordination with relevant authorities.

The successful candidate will ensure that effective security systems and SOPs are implemented and maintained across all assigned locations, identify potential security risks and take proactive measures to protect people, assets, materials, facilities and company operations
.

Job Responsibilities

Develop, implement, maintain, and regularly review security policies, SOPs, systems and operational procedures for factories and company premises.
Conduct regular security risk assessments to identify potential threats, vulnerabilities, and security gaps across factories, warehouses, sites and delivery points.
Develop appropriate security measures to protect company personnel, assets, raw materials, finished goods, machinery, equipment and facilities.
Assess security requirements and establish appropriate security deployment plans, duty posts, shift arrangements and coverage based on site-specific risks and operational needs.
Supervise and monitor security personnel and security supervisors to ensure discipline, alertness, proper conduct, grooming and effective performance.
Conduct regular security briefings, training, drills and counseling to improve the knowledge, discipline, alertness, and service quality of security personnel.
Establish and monitor effective gate security, access control, visitor management, vehicle checking, material movement control and employee entry/exit procedures.
Monitor CCTV surveillance, security patrols, gates, perimeter security and security posts to ensure effective protection of company premises.
Conduct regular visits and inspections of factories, warehouses, sites, premises and delivery points to identify security gaps and ensure compliance with established procedures.
Investigate and manage security incidents including theft, unauthorized access, loss of materials, security breaches, vandalism, sabotage, misconduct and other security violations.
Prepare detailed incident reports, investigation reports, inspection reports and security performance reports for management.

Requirements

Experience: 5-10 years
Education: bachelor of business administration (bba)
Skills: corporate security, security team leadership, security equipment operation, security operations, security management, security compliance, safetymanagement, security equipment, hr compliance

31 October 2026

jobs.description:
Program Manager — VITA Center of Excellence (COE)

Client:
Virginia Information Technologies Agency (VITA)
Team:
Center of Excellence (COE)
Location:
Richmond, VA area
Engagement Type:
12-month Contract
Number of Openings:
3

Position Overview

The VITA Center of Excellence is hiring Program Managers to serve as strategic coordinators for state agency initiatives — not day-to-day project managers. These roles help agencies plan, sequence, and navigate VITA's governance process from early project ideation through procurement, working backwards from an agency's goals to identify when contracts need to go before governance boards, when RFIs are needed, and when procurement needs to be engaged. Program Managers will also evaluate agency program and project maturity and help break large, multi-year agency efforts into well-scoped, discrete pieces of work.
Key Responsibilities

Serve as a strategic partner to state agencies, helping them navigate VITA governance (contract board submissions, RFIs, procurement engagement, etc.) rather than requiring agencies to master the governance framework themselves.
Break large, multi-year agency initiatives into discrete, well-scoped efforts (e.g., requirements generation, vendor procurement/sourcing, and architecture/design/build/test/evaluate phases) rather than managing an entire program as a single undifferentiated project.
Assess and track agency program/project maturity across areas such as planning, procurement/sourcing, execution, and staffing, and communicate how a proposed investment compares to an agency's demonstrated capability.
Flag governance risk early and advise COE and agency leadership on what needs to change before a project can responsibly move forward.
Operate proactively — flagging upcoming needs (e.g., anticipated subject matter expert requirements) well in advance — and reactively, stepping in quickly to help write contracts, staff an effort, and stabilize a struggling initiative.
Support procurement and vendor sourcing activities tied to agency initiatives.
Translate governance requirements and strategic vision into clear, actionable plans for both agency stakeholders and VITA leadership.

Required Qualifications

State government experience, ideally as a Program/Project Manager at a Virginia state agency (e.g., DMV or similar).
Direct, hands-on experience with VITA governance processes.
PMP certification.
Background in risk management.
Overseeing a Public Sector project over 5 Million Dollars or Private Sector Project over 10 Million
Strong critical thinking and communication skills.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have Qualifications

Experience using or implementing AI tools.
Private sector experience in addition to state government experience.

Additional Notes

Contract position; contract-to-hire may be considered to avoid re-interviewing down the line.
Candidates currently employed by or under contract with the Commonwealth of Virginia are not eligible.
Given the limited pool of Richmond-area candidates with both state agency and VITA governance experience, strong governance/process fit should be weighed alongside PMP and formal state tenure.
Rate card classification is still being finalized on the client side; competitive Richmond-market rates apply.

Benefits & Perks:

We’re a small team of dedicated thinkers, innovators, and problem-solvers. Our team is positive,
passionate, and collaborative.

C5ISR stands for Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance. You'll own delivery from start to finish, including cost, schedule, technical performance, risk, and P&L. You'll lead cross-functional matrixed teams and be the main point of contact for government customers in the U.S. and abroad.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the full program lifecycle for C5ISR systems: capture, planning, development, integration, test, deployment, sustainment, and close-out.
Set program goals, technical objectives, and KPIs to track progress and risk.
Oversee cost, schedule, technical performance, quality, and risk to keep the contract compliant and profitable.
Run program financial management, including the Earned Value Management System (EVMS) and other standard program controls.
Own P&L for your program(s) and drive results against revenue, margin, cash, and growth goals.
Coordinate engineering and operations to integrate sensors (radar, EO/IR), communications, ground control stations, and network operations.
Build and maintain risk management frameworks and risk registers. Drive mitigation and report risk status to executives and customers.
Act as the main point of contact for government customers and industry partners. Lead program reviews, technical interchange meetings, and status briefings.
Develop, negotiate, and administer contract deliverables, statements of work, schedules, budgets, and subcontractor agreements.
Work with Business Development and capture teams on proposals, funding strategy, and growth opportunities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline, business, or program management.
7+ years formally managing programs as a Program Manager.
5+ years working in Engineering and/or Operations.
Experience with U.S. and international government customers in defense markets.
A track record of leading and developing high-performing teams in a matrixed environment.
Hands-on experience putting program risk management frameworks in place.
U.S. citizenship, with an active security clearance or the ability to obtain one.
Able to work full-time, onsite in the Gilbert, AZ area.

Nice-to-have Qualifications

Master's degree or PMP certification.
C5ISR experience with Border/Homeland Security and military customers.
Experience with Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) contracts.
Knowledge of the government acquisition lifecycle and contract types (FFP, CPFF, T&M, IDIQ).
Working knowledge of FAR, DFARS, and HSAR compliance.
Experience with tactical radios, EO/IR, radar, networking, or computing platforms.
Experience supporting customer and government audits.
Familiarity with ERP systems, and experience building or improving program processes.

TOOLS & ENVIRONMENT

EVMS and program controls tools, ERP systems, and the Microsoft Office Suite.

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

You're a self-starter who brings urgency and discipline to complex programs with multiple agencies involved. You balance delivery against financial and risk performance, and you make decisions based on data. You can explain complex information clearly to engineers, executives, and government customers alike. You build strong working relationships with internal teams, suppliers, subcontractors, and partners. You hold yourself and your team to a high standard of compliance, mission assurance, and ethical conduct.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work is done in an office setting and may involve standing, sitting, bending, and climbing stairs.
You need to be able to lift 15–25 pounds.

This position will require a pre-employment background check and drug test to be administered by the clients preferred partners. All screening is required to be completed prior to start but will not be conducted until an offer has been made.
